title: Understand Clockwork installation and state compatibility
summary: Install or recover Clockwork program and provider selectors; understand retained state and coordinated broker refresh.
use_when: Program release selection, installation integrity, retained-state compatibility or rollback limits must be understood.
An operator must distinguish direct selector-only installation from coordinated broker refresh and explicit schema migration.
do_not_use_when: The request is the installation procedure; use clockwork.install.operate.
The caller intends destructive retained-state deletion or foreign selector takeover.
outcome: An exact understanding of owned installation and persistent compatibility guarantees.
effects: Installation copies supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned-path boundaries, writer locks and atomic selector replacements. Failed instructions retain completed changes without automatic rollback or recovery.

Direct installation may create missing current-user shared parent directories without changing the modes of existing parents; it writes only `~/.local/bin/clockwork`, `~/.local/bin/clockwork-install`, `providers/clockwork`, and Clockwork's installation tree, does not create or open the runtime database, and does not touch `org.clockwork.*` product plists.

Doctor initializes only an empty unversioned private schema-two Clockwork store, refuses foreign or unsupported schemas, runs SQLite `quick_check`, resolves the current executable, checks `/bin/launchctl`, and marks a retained `running` activation `lost` only after its recorded broker and any child are demonstrably absent.

Uninstall detaches only owned command, installer, provider, current, and previous selectors after refusing remaining Clockwork plists; when needed it may create an empty private Clockwork state root solely to share the deployment lock path, but it creates no runtime database and retains releases, database, runtime locks, logs, history, and product artifacts.

The Clockwork deployment command records complete prior binding intent, disables and drains each binding, publishes fixed runtime files, and restores only previously enabled selections with their exact definition digests. Disabled intent and failure incidents remain intact.

Direct installation copies release files and prepares resource directories without opening runtime state or running doctor. It performs no artifact-integrity, version-alignment, provider-discovery, or runtime-readiness validation.
authority: Clockwork packaging owns retained releases, fixed runtime files, current and previous archive selectors, public command and installer selectors, and only providers/clockwork.
Clockwork owns file placement and its explicit binding-refresh command. The Cell executor owns instruction order and process completion; it has no application-state or recovery authority.
The operator owns the choice to deploy, diagnose, roll back, or detach selectors and separately owns any destructive retained-state operation.

Product installers own definition and binding changes through the schedule contract. The Clockwork product command refreshes existing enabled broker plists without changing selected definition digests or approving incidents.
success: Direct installation publishes supplied program and provider selectors. Manifest deployment also completes the product-owned refresh of existing enabled broker bindings. Completion establishes no application readiness.
failure_and_recovery: Installation copies supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned-path boundaries, writer locks and atomic selector replacements. Failed instructions retain completed changes without automatic rollback or recovery.
Inspect current selectors and retained execution evidence after failure. Completed changes remain; no automatic restoration, detachment or application recovery follows.

If an installed program regression requires rollback, preserve its evidence and use a trusted tested clockwork-install recover --release with the canonical owned previous-release directory and an explicit Chancery reader; program rollback does not roll back a product binding.
Before detach, disable every binding and prove quiescence; the uninstaller's plist refusal does not prove that no manual child is already running.

An interrupted instruction has unknown effects. Inspect current Clockwork state and complete authorized product recovery separately from executor reconciliation and acknowledgement. Preserve binding intent and failure incidents.

An interrupted broker replacement retains clockwork-binding-intent.json in the deployment run and leaves unrestored schedules disabled. Inspect completed effects before explicitly restoring intent; no automatic recovery or incident approval occurs.
privacy: Release and provider bytes contain no definitions, product output, secrets, or activation history.

The retained private database and operational directories contain local paths, hashes, schedule metadata, process history, and possibly product-identifying information; packaging must neither copy nor print them.

interfaces.label: Deploy candidate
interfaces.invocation: <TESTED_CLOCKWORK_INSTALL> install --binary ABSOLUTE_PATH --bundle ABSOLUTE_BUNDLE_PATH --chancery ABSOLUTE_PATH [--home ABSOLUTE_HOME] [--expected-current absent|releases/ID]

does_not_authorize: Publishing a release, overwriting a foreign path, deleting retained Clockwork or product state, or pruning a release referenced by a generated plist or running activation.
Creating, migrating, switching, disabling, executing, or deleting a product binding as a side effect of direct Clockwork program installation.
Treating doctor, launchctl state, or installed version evidence as proof of product-domain success.

consumers.statement: The local operator may install, update, diagnose, roll back, or detach Clockwork's owned program and provider selectors while product schedules and retained runtime state remain separate.

preconditions.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
Uninstall requires every product binding disabled and quiescent and refuses if any `org.clockwork.*` plist remains.

inputs.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
Explicit migration requires product schedules and Clockwork commands to be quiescent and retained running rows/transitions settled.

outputs.statement: Public commands print plain text by default. --json selects the existing compact ok:true/data JSON envelope and coded ok:false/error JSON on stderr with exit one. Machine callers must pass --json.

Deployment retains an immutable release, replaces regular executable files at fixed runtime paths, and publishes command and provider selectors, doctor returns bounded local evidence plus a lost-recovery count, and uninstall removes only validated Clockwork-owned public selectors.

data_semantics.statement: Current and previous select owned program releases; they are independent of stable product bindings and their selected immutable product definitions.
An absent runtime database after program deployment is expected, while retained runtime state after selector detach is deliberate and is not an uninstall failure.

identity_and_units.statement: An opaque UUID identifies each prepared installed release. Program release, package version, provider contract, runtime schema and definition digest are separate identities. Runtime hashes remain part of the independent scheduling boundary.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.
No future launchd delivery, product readiness, release retention duration, or program availability percentage is promised.

access.statement: Installation copies supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned-path boundaries, writer locks and atomic selector replacements. Failed instructions retain completed changes without automatic rollback or recovery.
Remote installation, root or system-wide installation, direct retained-state deletion, and takeover of another provider or command selector are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Installation copies supplied program and provider files and reads release metadata without version, artifact-integrity or provider-discovery validation. It retains owned-path boundaries, writer locks and atomic selector replacements. Failed instructions retain completed changes without automatic rollback or recovery.

Direct program installation and recovery require disabled bindings and settle admitted activations without changing selected definitions or halt state; doctor may initialize only an empty unversioned schema-two store and recover only demonstrably stale running rows; uninstall detaches selectors only after plist absence and retains program releases and runtime state.

Migration takes a schema gate and changes schema transactionally in place without rewriting definition identities or selecting schedules. Older binaries cannot open schema two. Recovery requires compatible program/product releases with newer incident evidence preserved; there is no reverse schema operation.

Cell-install-v4 publishes regular runtime files with atomic per-file replacements. Public executable symlinks target runtime; directory/provider symlinks follow current. Current and previous retain archive selections. Recovery republishes compatible retained bytes at the same runtime paths; existing fixed broker plists keep that path, while legacy archive-bound plists require refresh.

operational_limits.statement: Installation manages one current-user product command selector, one installer selector, one provider selector, and one private immutable program-release tree and one fixed runtime tree of regular files; it starts no daemon. Coordinated deployment retains binding intent, disables and drains all bindings, publishes runtime files, then restores only previously enabled selections.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Program release, package version, provider release, definition manifest, database schema and binding identity have independent meanings. File placement performs no version-compatibility inference.
No automatic release pruning, retention horizon, cross-version state migration window, or deprecation period is promised.

This complete bundle uses provider schema four and requires a reader that validates/discovers that schema; Chancery 0.8 supplies the interfaces. SQLite schema two and old definition semantics are independent.

Pre-runtime Clockwork installation metadata remains readable. Direct recovery rejects targets older than cell-install-v4 because their broker requires an archive execution path and cannot admit schema-three definitions. Historical behavior requires a runtime-aware rebuilt candidate.

reliances.statement: Installation copies program and provider files and reads release metadata. Chancery validation and discovery are separate operations and do not gate publication.

Direct program installation, program rollback and selector detach invoke no model, network service, Nucleus job or product runner; coordinated binding refresh can request run-at-load work under the product contract.
